problemStatement.formal: For countably infinite sets (A_i) with |A_i intersect A_j| != 2 for i != j, find the smallest cardinal C such that the union can always be colored with at most C colors and no A_i is monochromatic.
problemStatement.plain: Erdos #603 asks for the least number of colors needed to avoid monochromatic members in countably infinite set families whose pairwise intersections are never of size two.
whyMatters: This is a hypergraph-coloring problem for infinite set systems with a forbidden intersection size.
The Lean file proves basic lower, countable-index upper, and disjoint-family special-case results.
The exact finite-versus-countable answer remains open and one related Komjath theorem is axiomatized.
